notes:
I couldn't write the Proverbs 24 notes. None of the sources loaded properly, and I can't make any more lookups in this session, so I have nothing from the approved sites to work from.

**What happened:** I tried to load five verse-by-verse sources at once: Enduring Word, Gill and Ellicott on StudyLight, Precept Austin, and the Pulpit Commentary on BibleHub. The responses came back in a format my code wasn't expecting. Before I could see what any page contained, I hit the session's limit on lookups. I didn't read any page text, so I have nothing I can honestly report or cite.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say. Writing the notes from my own memory of these commentaries would break that rule, so I haven't.

**What to do next:** In a new session I'd start by checking that these five pages load correctly. If they do, I'd go on to:

- **Protestant differences:** desiringgod.org, gty.org, ligonier.org, thegospelcoalition.org, wesley.nnu.edu (Wesley's notes), 1517.org and spurgeon.org.
- **Other views:**
  - netbible.org notes: the Hebrew wording of vv. 5, 7, 9 and 10, the scale image for God weighing hearts in v. 12, God's wrath turning away in v. 18, and whether v. 27 is about marriage.
  - Catholic and Orthodox readings: newadvent.org (Church Fathers on "seven times" in v. 16 and on rescuing the condemned in v. 11) and catholic.com.
  - gotquestions.org, for v. 16 and how it gets applied in popular teaching.

Doing it in small batches would avoid running out of lookups again.
